Debased

dih-BAYST · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Debased is reduced in quality, value, or moral standing; degraded.

Longtime readers said the literary prize had grown debased after years of sponsors quietly pushing their own favorite authors onto the shortlist.

Worked Example

Once celebrated for its independent bookstores, the neighborhood's reputation grew debased after a wave of tacky souvenir shops moved in.

Nothing was physically destroyed -- the neighborhood's standing simply declined in quality and character, exactly what debased describes.

How Debased Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

degraded

degraded: lowered in quality, character, or condition

diminished

diminished: lessened in size, number, or importance; debased means lowered in quality or purity, as when something cheaper is mixed in

Antonyms

refined

refined: improved through a careful process; purified

elevated

elevated: raised to a higher quality or status

How Strong Is It? — watered-down → debased → ruined

watered-down vs. debased

watered-down vs. debased: Something watered-down has been mildly diluted, a smaller loss of quality than debased.

ruined vs. debased

ruined vs. debased: Something ruined has been destroyed entirely, a more extreme loss than debased.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: down (Latin)

root — base

root — base: low, of little value (English, from Latin bassus, "low")

Put it together

Put it together: Debased combines de- ("down") with the everyday word base ("low" or "of little value") -- to debase something is literally to bring it down to a lower, baser condition.

Use the root in a new word: base

Use the root in a new word: base: He was ashamed of the base motives -- pure greed -- behind his decision.

Root Check

Word Choice

Debased describes something -- a currency, a set of values, a public debate, a piece of jewelry -- that has been lowered in quality or worth. It's less extreme than depraved, which describes active, deliberate wickedness rather than reduced quality.
